question.text: The principle of 'tax neutrality' in AIF pooling means:

answer.text: The fund pays no taxes at all
The pooled structure should not put investors in a worse tax position compared to investing individually
Investors get tax refunds from the government

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax neutrality (p. 100) means the pooled structure should not place an investor in a comparatively adverse tax position relative to investing individually. Chapter 12 (pp. 253-258) supports Category I/II pass-through treatment for non-business income and fund-level taxation for business income. The Trap: Option A confuses neutrality with full exemption. Option C is unrelated to pooling. Option D overstates the exemption available to AIF income. Note: Category I/II pass-through treatment for non-business income is workbook-supported; broader comparisons or selling-point claims about Category III should be separately sourced before being relied upon.
